descriptionChirho: A fellow human being, especially one with whom one has social or covenantal obligation; used substantivally as 'the neighbor' in the love command (Mt 19:19; 22:39; Mk 12:31; Lk 10:27,29,36; Rom 13:9-10; Gal 5:14; Jas 2:8). Translations consistently render as a person noun: eng 'neighbor,' spa 'prójimo' (fellow person), arb قَريبَكَ (qaribaka, your near one), hin पड़ोसी (padosi, neighbor), kor 이웃 (i-ut, neighbor), swa 'jirani' (neighbor). The Parable of the Good Samaritan (Lk 10) expands this concept beyond ethnic or geographic proximity.

Spatially close; in the vicinity of a place or object. Used as a preposition of place indicating physical nearness (Acts 27:8, of a city near a harbor). Translations shift to spatial language: eng 'near,' spa 'cerca' (close by), arb قَرِيبَةٍ (qaribatin, nearby/proximate), hin निकट (nikat, close/near), kor 가까이 (gakkai, close by), swa 'karibu na' (close to). This adverbial/prepositional sense preserves the original spatial root from which the substantive 'neighbor' developed.
